name: Python Basics - Your First Program
description: Learn to install Python and write your first 'Hello World' program step by step

character.welcomeMessage:
আছস? Ready to learn Python? 🐍
Don't worry, I'll guide you through every step!
Let's make coding fun and easy!
character.completionMessage:
🎉 Congratulations! You've written your first Python program!
You're officially a Python programmer now!
আছস? wasn't that amazing? 😊

steps.instruction: First, let's get Python! Open your web browser and go to python.org/downloads
steps.detailedInstruction: Click on your web browser icon (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, etc.) and type 'python.org/downloads' in the address bar, then press Enter.
steps.successMessage: Perfect! You opened a browser. Now navigate to python.org/downloads to get Python.

errorMessages.timeout: Take your time! When you're ready, open any web browser.
errorMessages.wrongAction: Hmm, that's not quite right. Try opening a web browser first.

hints: Look for browser icons on your taskbar or desktop
Common browsers: Chrome (colorful circle), Firefox (orange fox), Edge (blue 'e')
You can also search for 'browser' in your start menu

steps.instruction: Download Python for your operating system (Windows/Mac/Linux)
steps.detailedInstruction: On the Python downloads page, click the big yellow 'Download Python' button for your system. The website will automatically detect your operating system.
steps.successMessage: Great! Python installer downloaded successfully. Let's install it next!

errorMessages.timeout: Downloads can take time. Check your Downloads folder or try again.
errorMessages.wrongFile: Make sure you download the Python installer, not something else.

hints: Look for a big yellow button that says 'Download Python'
The download might go to your Downloads folder
File size is usually 20-30 MB

steps.instruction: Run the Python installer and follow the setup wizard
steps.detailedInstruction: Find the downloaded Python installer file (usually in Downloads folder) and double-click it. IMPORTANT: Check 'Add Python to PATH' before clicking Install!
steps.successMessage: Excellent! Python is installed. Now let's test if it's working properly.

errorMessages.timeout: Installation can take a few minutes. Let it finish completely.
errorMessages.pathError: Remember to check 'Add Python to PATH' during installation!

hints: Double-click the downloaded file to start installation
Always check 'Add Python to PATH' checkbox
Choose 'Install Now' for default settings
You might need administrator permission

steps.detailedInstruction: On Windows: Press Windows key + R, type 'cmd' and press Enter. On Mac: Press Cmd + Space, type 'terminal'. On Linux: Press Ctrl + Alt + T.
steps.successMessage: Perfect! Command line is open. Now let's check if Python is installed correctly.

errorMessages.timeout: No rush! Open the command line when you're ready.
errorMessages.wrongApp: Make sure you open Command Prompt, PowerShell, or Terminal.

hints: Windows: Search for 'cmd' or 'command prompt' in start menu
Windows: You can also use PowerShell
Mac: Search for 'terminal' in Spotlight
The window should show a prompt where you can type commands

steps.detailedInstruction: In the command prompt/terminal, type exactly: python --version (with two dashes) and press Enter. You should see the Python version number.
steps.successMessage: Awesome! Python is working perfectly. Time to write your first program!

errorMessages.commandNotFound: If you get 'command not found', Python might not be in PATH. Try 'python3 --version'
errorMessages.timeout: Type the command and press Enter. Don't worry if it takes a moment!

hints: Type exactly: python --version
Make sure to use two dashes: --
Press Enter after typing
If 'python' doesn't work, try 'python3'

steps.instruction: Create a new file called 'hello.py' on your Desktop
steps.detailedInstruction: Go to your Desktop, right-click in an empty space, select 'New' > 'Text Document' (Windows) or use any text editor. Name the file 'hello.py' - the .py extension is important!
steps.successMessage: Perfect! You created hello.py. Now let's add some Python code to it!

errorMessages.timeout: Take your time creating the file. Remember to name it 'hello.py'
errorMessages.wrongExtension: Make sure the file ends with .py, not .txt!

hints: Right-click on Desktop > New > Text Document
Change the name from 'hello.txt' to 'hello.py'
The .py extension tells the computer it's a Python file
You can also use Notepad, VS Code, or any text editor

steps.instruction: Open hello.py and type: print('Hello, World!')
steps.detailedInstruction: Double-click hello.py to open it in a text editor. Delete any existing content and type exactly: print('Hello, World!') - pay attention to the quotes and parentheses!
steps.successMessage: Excellent! You wrote your first Python code. Now let's run it and see the magic!

errorMessages.timeout: Open the file and add the code when you're ready.
errorMessages.syntaxError: Make sure you typed: print('Hello, World!') exactly as shown.

hints: Double-click hello.py to open it
Type exactly: print('Hello, World!')
Use single quotes: ' not "
Don't forget the parentheses: ( )
Save the file when done (Ctrl+S)

steps.instruction: In terminal, navigate to Desktop and run: python hello.py
steps.detailedInstruction: In your command prompt/terminal, type 'cd Desktop' to go to Desktop folder, then type 'python hello.py' to run your program. You should see 'Hello, World!' printed!
steps.successMessage:
🎉 CONGRATULATIONS! You just ran your first Python program!
You're officially a Python programmer now!

errorMessages.fileNotFound: Make sure you're in the Desktop folder: type 'cd Desktop' first
errorMessages.pythonError: If you get an error, check that hello.py contains: print('Hello, World!')

hints: First type: cd Desktop (to go to Desktop folder)
Then type: python hello.py (to run your program)
You should see 'Hello, World!' appear!
If 'python' doesn't work, try 'python3 hello.py'
